definitions.explanation: a Japanese rice bowl dish consisting of chicken and egg simmered in a sweet soy-based sauce, served over rice

examples.japanese: お{昼|ひる}に{親子丼|おやこどん}を{食|た}べた。
{親子丼|おやこどん}は{卵|たまご}がふわふわなのがおいしい。
examples.english: Oyakodon is delicious when the egg is fluffy.

examples.japanese: {定食屋|ていしょくや}で{親子丼|おやこどん}を{注文|ちゅうもん}した。
examples.english: I ordered oyakodon at a set meal restaurant.

notes:
NAME ORIGIN:
{親|おや} (parent) + {子|こ} (child) + {丼|どん} (rice bowl) → "parent and child bowl"
The name comes from the combination of chicken (parent) and egg (child).

INGREDIENTS:
- {鶏肉|とりにく} (chicken)
- {卵|たまご} (egg)
- {玉|たま}ねぎ (onion)
- {醤油|しょうゆ} (soy sauce)
- みりん (sweet cooking sake)
- {出汁|だし} (dashi broth)
- ご{飯|はん} (rice)

COOKING TIP:
The egg should be slightly runny ({半熟|はんじゅく}) for the best texture.

RELATED {丼|どんぶり} DISHES:
- カツ{丼|どん} (pork cutlet rice bowl)
- {牛丼|ぎゅうどん} (beef rice bowl)
- {天丼|てんどん} (tempura rice bowl)
- {海鮮丼|かいせんどん} (seafood rice bowl)
